RSVPs are required for all who plan to attend in-person. If you plan to attend in-person, sign up in advance using this form: (https://tinyurl.com/PDCmeetingform) and indicate your attendance in-person no later than 3:00 p.m., Friday, November 13.

rows.short_title: New York City Indirect Source Rule 'WISER' Program
rows.additional_description_1:
New York City Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) proposes to implement a Warehouse Indirect Source Emissions Reduction (WISER) local law that would require large warehouse operators to reduce mobile sources of pollution and/or mitigate the impact of the air pollution associated with their operations in New York City. In accordance with the State Environmental Quality Review Act (SEQRA) (Section 8-0113, Article 8 of the Environmental Conservation Law) as set forth in 6 NYCRR Part 617, and the City Environmental Quality Review (CEQR) process, as set forth in Executive Order 91 of 1977 and its amendments, DEP is hereby issuing Notice of Positive Declaration, Intent to Prepare a Draft Environmental Impact Statement, Lead Agency Declaration and Draft Scope of Work.

DEP will hold a virtual public scoping meeting to receive public comments on the Draft Scope of Work on November 17, 2026, at 4:00 PM. The Draft Scope of Work, which provides a summary description of the Program and the methodologies to be used in preparing the Draft EIS impact analyses, is available on the DEP website at https://www.nyc.gov/site/dep/about/environmental-reviews.page. You may register for the virtual public meeting at: https://bit.ly/4egU5lY. Comments on the Draft Scope of Work may be presented at the meeting or submitted in writing or by email to:

Dana Taplin, Project Manager

NYC Department of Environmental Protection, Bureau of Environmental Planning and Analysis

59-17 Junction Boulevard, 4th Floor

Flushing, NY 11373

dtaplin@dep.nyc.gov

Written comments on the Draft Scope of Work will be accepted until December 17, 2026, at 4:00 PM. DEP will subsequently issue a Final Scope of Work, which will include responses to written comments and comments received during the public meeting and may incorporate revisions in response to comments received.

rows.short_title: New York City Housing Authority Board Meeting
rows.additional_description_1:
The next Board Meeting of the New York City Housing Authority is scheduled for Wednesday, November 18, 2026 at 10:00 A.M. in the Ceremonial Room on the 5th Floor of 90 Church Street, New York, New York 10007 (unless otherwise noted). This Board Meeting will also be streamed live on NYCHA's YouTube Channel at https://www.youtube.com/c/nycha and NYCHA's Website at https://www.nyc.gov/site/nycha/about/board-meetings.page

These Board Meetings are open to the public. To provide comment in-person, all speakers are required to pre-register, at least forty-five (45) minutes before the scheduled Board Meeting. Comments are limited to the items on the Calendar. Speaking time will be limited to three (3) minutes. The public comment period will conclude upon all speakers being heard or at the expiration of thirty (30) minutes allotted for public comment, whichever occurs first. Comments may also be provided to the Office of the Corporate Secretary by e-mail at corporate.secretary@nycha.nyc.gov or by mail at 90 Church Street, 5th Floor, New York NY 10007.

Please note that the Minutes for prior Board Meetings and the Calendar for the upcoming Board Meeting may be obtained by visiting the NYCHA Website at https://www.nyc.gov/site/nycha/about/board-meetings.page. Copies of the Calendar may also be picked up at the Office of the Corporate Secretary at 90 Church Street, 5th Floor, New York, NY, 10007, no earlier than twenty-four (24) hours before the upcoming Board Meeting. Copies of the Draft Minutes may also be picked up at the Office of the Corporate Secretary, no earlier than 3:00 P.M. on the Tuesday following the Board Meeting. Any changes to the schedule will be posted on this webpage and via social media, to the extent practicable, at a reasonable time before the Board Meeting.

Any person requiring a reasonable accommodation, including wheelchair accessibility or large print availability, to participate in the Board Meeting should contact the Office of the Corporate Secretary by e-mail at corporate.secretary@nycha.nyc.gov or by phone at (212) 306-6088, no later than 5:00 P.M., seven (7) calendar days before the Board Meeting.

For additional information regarding Board Meetings, please contact the Office of the Corporate Secretary by e-mail at corporate.secretary@nycha.nyc.gov or by phone at (212) 306-6088.

rows.short_title: 1678 Park Avenue
rows.additional_description_1:
PLEASE TAKE NOTICE that a public hearing will be held on November 18, 2026 at 11:00 a.m. The Public Hearing will be held at The Harlem Library, 224 East 125th Street, Manhattan at which time and place those wishing to be heard will be given an opportunity to be heard concerning the proposed deed and land disposition agreement amendments described below

 

Pursuant to Section 1802(6)(j) of the Charter, the Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) has proposed amendments to the terms and conditions of the sale of certain real property previously conveyed by the City of New York (City), located in the Borough of Manhattan and known as:   

 

Address                                          Block/Lot(s) 

 

1678 Park Avenue                          1745/134

                                                       (FKA p/o Lot 32, Lot 33-39, p/o Lot 41)                                                            

1678 Park Avenue was conveyed by the City to NYC Partnership Housing Development Fund Company, Inc. on December 13, 2001, pursuant to a deed and land disposition agreement (LDA). The deed and LDA require compliance with the original Milbank Frawley Circle-East Urban Renewal Plan (Original Plan), approved by the City Planning Commission on August 19, 1992 (C920139HUM) and the New York City Council on October 8, 1992 (Reso. No. 920), which prohibits residential development within 100 feet of Park Avenue and restricts the sites to parking. On November 30, 2017, the Original Plan was amended (Second Amendment) by the New York City Council (Reso. No. 1743) to permit residential use within 100 feet of Park Avenue.

 

The sponsor now intends to develop a proposed project consisting of one 100% affordable residential building financed by NYCHA that will include 222 total units and 80 parking spaces (the Project).

 

To facilitate the Project, HPD intends to modify the deed and LDA. The site is located in the Milbank Frawley Circle East Urban Renewal Area and is identified as a portion of Site 37A within the Plan. The deed and LDA associated with the parcel require compliance with the Original Plan, which specifically prohibits development within 100 feet of Park Avenue. HPD intends to amend the deed and LDA  to remove the restrictions limiting the use of the parcel to parking and require compliance with the Second Amendment, which will be in effect until December 14, 2057, and replace these restrictions with new restrictions that would require that 1678 Park Avenue be developed as a 100% affordable project.

 

A public file containing copies of the calendar document and other public documents will be made available to Manhattan Community Board 11 for public review at the office of Community Board 11 no later than twenty (20) days prior to the public hearing. 

 

To make a request for accommodation, such as sign language interpretation services, please contact the Mayors Office of Contract Services (MOCS) via e-mail at disabilityaffairs@mocs.nyc.gov or via phone at (212) 298-0734. TDD users should call Verizon relay services. Any person requiring reasonable accommodation for the public hearing should contact MOCS at least three (3) business days in advance of the hearing to ensure availability.

rows.additional_description_1:
PLEASE TAKE NOTICE that a public hearing will be held on November 19, 2026, at 11:30 A.M. The public hearing will be held at 125th Street Library, 224 East 125th Street, Manhattan, or as soon thereafter as the matter may be reached on the calendar, at which time and place those wishing to be heard will be given an opportunity to be heard concerning the proposed amendments to a deed and land disposition agreement identified below.

 

Pursuant to Section 695(2)(b) of the General Municipal Law and Section 1802(6)(j) of the Charter, the Department of Housing Preservation and Development ('HPD') of the City of New York ('City') proposed amendments to the terms and conditions of the sale of certain real property previously conveyed by the City of New York (collectively, 'Disposition Area') in the Borough of Manhattan:

 

                Address                            Block/Lots         Community District

                53 East 110th Street            1616/123                  11

                304 East 126th Street           1802/47                    11

                201 East 120th Street           1785/1                      11

                204 West 121st Street          1926/35                    10

 

Under HPD's Division of Property Disposition and Finance program, City-owned vacant and/or occupied multifamily residential buildings may be purchased and gut-rehabilitated by a designated sponsor in order to create affordable rental housing units with a range of affordability. Construction and permanent financing is provided through loans from private institutional lenders and from public sources, including HPD.

 

On November 23, 2020, the City conveyed the Disposition Area to CLT East Harlem/El Barrio Community Land Trust Housing Development Fund Corporation. The deed and land disposition agreement recorded against the Premises requires compliance with a project summary approved by the Council requiring the development of approximately 36 rental dwelling units, two commercial spaces, and one community facility space. While it was originally intended that there would be commercial spaces in the project, it is now being developed with three community facility spaces and approximately 38 rental dwelling units. On July 16, 2026 (Res. No. 579), the Council approved an amended project summary reflecting these new conditions, and the deed and land disposition agreement will be amended to reflect these changes.

                                                                                                              

A public file containing copies of the calendar document and other public documents will be made available to Manhattan Community Board 11 for public review at the office of Manhattan Community Board 11 no later than twenty (20) days prior to the public hearing.

 

The hearing location is accessible to individuals using wheelchairs or other mobility devices. For further information on accessibility or to make a request for accommodation, such as sign language interpretation services, please contact the Mayors Office of Contract Services (MOCS) via e-mail at disabilityaffairs@mocs.nyc.gov or via phone at (212) 788-0010.  TDD users should call Verizon relay services.  Any person requiring reasonable accommodation for the public hearing should contact MOCS at least three (3) business days in advance of the hearing to ensure availability.

Pursuant to Section 695(2)(b) of the General Municipal Law and Section 1802(6)(j) of the Charter, the Department of Housing Preservation and Development ('HPD') of the City of New York ('City') has proposed the sale of the following City-owned property (collectively, 'Disposition Area') in the Borough of Brooklyn:

Address                                                                          Block/Lot

516 Bergen Street                                                         Block 1143 Lot 25                                                                                                        

Under HPD's Extremely Low and Low Income Affordability Program, sponsors purchase City-owned or privately owned land or vacant buildings and construct multifamily buildings in order to create affordable rental housing.  Construction and permanent financing is provided through loans from private institutional lenders and from public sources including HPD, the New York City Housing Development Corporation, the State of New York, and the federal government.  Additional funding may also be provided from the syndication of low-income housing tax credits.  The newly constructed buildings provide rental housing to low-income families with a range of incomes from 30% to 80% of the Area Median Income (AMI).  Projects may include tiers of units with rents affordable to households earning up to 100% of AMI.  Subject to project underwriting, up to 30% of the units may be rented to formerly homeless families and individuals.

Under the proposed project, the City will sell the Disposition Area to 516 Bergen Green Housing Development Fund Company, Inc. ('Sponsor') for the nominal price of one dollar per tax lot.  The Sponsor will also deliver an enforcement note and mortgage for the remainder of the appraised value (Land Debt).  The Sponsor will then construct one building containing approximately 111 rental dwelling units, plus one unit for a superintendent and community facility space on the Disposition Area. The Sponsor will provide approximately 23 replacement parking spaces for HPD.

The Land Debt or the Citys capital subsidy may be repayable out of resale or refinancing profits for a period of at least thirty (30) years following completion of construction.  The remaining balance, if any, may be forgiven at the end of the term.

The appraisal and the proposed Land Disposition Agreement and Project Summary are available for public examination by emailing Margaret Carey at careym@hpd.nyc.gov on business days during business hours.

To make a request for accommodation, such as sign language interpretation services, please contact the Mayors Office of Contract Services (MOCS) via e-mail at disabilityaffairs@mocs.nyc.gov or via phone at (212) 298-0734.  TDD users should call Verizon relay services.  Any person requiring reasonable accommodation for the public hearing should contact MOCS at least three (3) business days in advance of the hearing to ensure availability.

rows.additional_description_1:
NOTICE OF A FRANCHISE AND CONCESSION REVIEW COMMITTEE (FCRC) PUBLIC HEARING to be held on 12/7/2026, at 2:30PM at 255 Greenwich Street, 8th Floor, New York, NY 10007 relative to the proposed amendment of the Public Communications Structures franchise agreement between the City of New York and CityBridge, LLC.

The proposed amendment would extend the term of the franchise agreement to March 22, 2035, while also amending various other terms, including a modification to the minimum number of structures that must be deployed and an increase of the minimum fee due to the City of New York.

The public may participate in the public hearing by attending and providing testimony. Written testimony may be submitted in advance of the hearing electronically to fcrc@mocs.nyc.gov. All written testimony must be received by 12/7/2026.

 

A draft copy of the proposed franchise agreement amendment may be obtained at no cost any of the following ways:

  1. Submitting a written electronic request to the NYC Office of Technology and Innovation (OTI) at franchiseopportunities@oti.nyc.gov from 11/20/2026 through 12/4/2026.
  2. Downloading from 11/20/2026 through 12/7/2026 on OTIs website. To download a draft copy of the proposed franchise agreement amendment, visit https://www.nyc.gov/content/oti/pages/franchises.
  3. By submitting a written request by mail to NYC Office of Technology & Innovation, 2 MetroTech Center, P-1 Level Mailroom. Written requests must be received by 12/4/2026. For mail-in requests, please include your name, return address, and a request for a specific calendar item.

 

The agenda and related documentation for the hearing will be posted on the MOCS website at https://www.nyc.gov/site/mocs/opportunities/franchises-concessions.page. 

 

For further information on accessibility or to make a request for accommodations, such as sign language interpretation services, please contact the Mayors Office of Contract Services (MOCS) via e-mail at DisabilityAffairs@mocs.nyc.gov or via phone at (212) 298-0800. Any person requiring reasonable accommodation for the public hearing should contact MOCS at least five (5) business days in advance of the hearing to ensure availability.
